data.rootCause: The render is visually strong in the opening and prep beats, but it fails as a finished commercial because the actual timeline is overloaded with repeated prep frames, missing the planned multi-beat progression, and the audio/exec layer appears unfinished. The biggest issue is that the rendered reel does not match the intended fast 15s structure: it hangs too long on the same chef-roll shot, then turns into a static text-heavy sequence with weak CTA differentiation and no visible proof of designed sound or transitions.

issues.problem: The reel lingers far too long on the same rolling/prep shot, creating a dead middle and killing momentum.
issues.fix: Cut the prep beat to a single concise section and move immediately into the plated hero or ingredient detail.

issues.problem: The latter half visually repeats the same chef-and-sushi setup with minimal change, so the story stalls instead of progressing.
issues.fix: Reorder to create hook > craft > ingredient > hero > bite, with each shot offering a distinct visual idea.

issues.problem: The executable timeline indicates no realized SFX or speed ramps, and the render feels musically flat/unfinished.
issues.fix: Add distinct impact/reveal/CTA SFX and a clearer music rise-drop pattern to make it feel like a commercial.

issues.problem: Text is overused and sits too long on-screen, becoming repetitive instead of premium.
issues.fix: Use fewer words, fewer full-screen text moments, and tighter timing so each line lands once.

issues.problem: Brand presence is weak; the reel feels like generic sushi content until the last second.
issues.fix: Bring the KAIRO name into a cleaner end card or earlier branded lockup so the restaurant is memorable.

issues.problem: The ending is not instantly understood as a visit action; it reads more like a lingering prep frame with text than a decisive offer.
issues.fix: End on the bite/reaction with a clear, high-contrast CTA line and, if possible, a branded tag or location cue.
